body:
Hello App Review,

I have prepared a substantive revision, version 1.0 build 2, after the 4.3/4.2.6 rejection. It is selected in the draft with revised metadata and ten screenshots per device. WakeMeUp-Build2-Demo.mp4 is attached to App Review Information.

1. Functionality/problem: Wake Me Up connects a scheduled native AlarmKit alarm to an ordered morning route of up to five steps. Thirteen choices cover push-ups, squats, dancing, marching, stretch, breathing, sun taps, typed maths, memory, typed intention, a destination code, light and a drink. Focus tasks require correct responses; destination codes match local fingerprints. Camera/motion estimates and labelled self-report alternatives are optional. Completed real alarm routes create local journal entries; practice does not. Optional native follow-up alerts confirm the same entry. Weekly, dated and work/rest schedules support skip-next, one-time time changes, days off and pauses. Special calendar plans schedule fourteen upcoming dates and show their horizon. iOS retains its Stop control; exercise is never forced.

2. Audience: People who repeatedly dismiss/snooze alarms, including students and workers with changing wake schedules, who want a comfortable start. Guided, gentle alternatives work without camera/motion permission. The app makes no medical or guaranteed wake-up claim.

3. Gap: Public alarm-app reviews and community discussions highlighted schedule exceptions, sound choice, morning transitions and staying awake. It combines reusable routes, destination matching, follow-up confirmation, clear completion modes and private history without login. These qualitative findings are not beta feedback or a claim of exclusivity.

4. Testing: No external beta feedback has been collected yet. Build 2 is processed in TestFlight. Validation includes 21 unit tests, nine UI checks on each phone/tablet simulator, signed native alarm/snooze/follow-up flows, and a passing local StoreKit purchase/restore check. It led to compatible AAC audio and an iPad keyboard fix. Real-device custom sound, camera/motion and external TestFlight feedback remain outstanding. The silent simulator demo retains original timing with cuts; fifteen-second DEBUG alarms use default sound.

5. Standalone/suite: It is standalone, with no shared subscription or required companion app. Relevant portfolio distinctions: Daily Check Widget manages daily checklists; My Great Lists manages general lists; Pace Up: Walk Time Capsules records walks; PeakInterval: HIIT Timer runs workout/focus intervals; Ai Meal/Food Tracker logs nutrition; Next Birthday: Moments & Plans organizes celebrations; Think in Numbers trains arithmetic; Motivational Dream presents quotes. Wake Me Up centers on scheduled wake alarms and their recoverable morning routes.

6. Consolidation: Alarm authorization, wake schedules, snooze, route recovery and follow-ups form a separate primary workflow from interval training, checklists or walk tracking.

7. Sharing: This project has app-specific alarm, calendar, route, challenge and journal source. It uses familiar SwiftUI/StoreKit patterns and Apple frameworks. Exact-file comparison found no identical Swift files across 21 other available local repositories, or identical bundled artwork/audio candidates. This comparison does not cover generic patterns or every historic source.

8. Third parties: No commercial app template, third-party runtime SDK, ads/analytics SDK or developer backend is included. Source and artwork were authored with AI assistance for this project. Three instrumental tracks were generated/downloaded under Suno Premier; six presets are excerpts. Apple frameworks provide native capabilities and payments.

9. Ownership: This is my own app for my developer portfolio, submitted directly through Oana Rinaldi's account, with my repository and website; it is not a client template submission.

Please evaluate the revision and advise if further evidence is needed.
Oana Rinaldi
